questions.subject: PHYSICS_II
questions.learningObjective: compute the electrostatic force between two charges
questions.stem: Two point charges of 3 microcoulombs and 5 microcoulombs are 0.2 metres apart. What is the magnitude of the electrostatic force between them, in newtons? Use k = 8.99e9. Report the number only.
questions.explanation: Coulomb's law gives F = k q1 q2 / r squared, so 8.99e9 times 3e-6 times 5e-6 divided by 0.04 equals 3371.25 newtons. Using r instead of r squared, or forgetting to convert microcoulombs to coulombs, both give wrong answers by orders of magnitude.
questions.hint: F = k q1 q2 / r^2. Convert microcoulombs to coulombs.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_II
questions.learningObjective: compute the electrostatic force between two charges
questions.stem: Point charges of 2.0 microcoulombs and 4.0 microcoulombs are separated by 0.10 m. What is the electrostatic force magnitude in newtons? Use k = 8.99e9.
questions.explanation: F = k q1 q2 / r^2 = 8.99e9 * 2e-6 * 4e-6 / 0.10^2 = 7.192 N. Forgetting to square the distance gives 0.7192 N.
questions.hint: Convert microcoulombs to coulombs and square the separation.
